name: RATE
description: RATE returns the periodic interest rate for an annuity based on the number of periods, payment amount, present value, and future value.
tldr: Calculates the interest rate per period of a loan or investment.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: 0 = end of period (default), 1 = beginning of period.

basicExample.explanation: A $20,000 loan paid back with $400 monthly payments for 5 years has a monthly interest rate of about 0.63%.

advancedExamples.title: Annual interest rate
advancedExamples.description: Convert the monthly rate to an annual rate
advancedExamples.explanation: Multiply the monthly rate by 12 to estimate the nominal annual rate.

howItWorks: RATE uses an iterative method to find the interest rate that makes the net present value of the cash flows equal to zero. If the formula fails to converge, try a different guess.

howToSteps.name: Calculate
howToSteps.text: Press Enter to get the result.

limitations: May fail to converge for unusual cash-flow patterns; use a guess value to help.
Returns the periodic rate, not the annual rate.

commonErrors.cause: The formula cannot converge to a solution.
Result is monthly but was interpreted as annual.
commonErrors.fix: Multiply by the number of periods per year.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: RATE works identically in Google Sheets.
googleSheetsEquivalent.notes: Same syntax and behavior as Excel.

faq.question: How do I convert RATE to an annual rate?
faq.answer: Multiply the periodic rate by the number of periods per year.

faq.question: What is the guess argument?
faq.answer: It is an initial estimate for the iterative solver. Default is 10%.

faq.question: Can RATE return multiple rates?
faq.answer: No, it returns the first rate it finds. For multiple IRRs, use IRR or MIRR.
